reason: The hypothesis assumes FeNiCrMn has low SFE and that this drives twin-mediated hardening, but no cited evidence measures SFE or twinning in FeNiCrMn. E2 reports twinning and hardening in Al0.3CoCrFeNi, a different alloy with Al and Co, and E3 discusses an fcc→hcp transition in Cantor alloy, not FeNiCrMn. The key premises are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: FeNiCrMn has inherently low stacking fault energy (SFE) comparable to CoCrFeMnNi
Low SFE inhibits cross-slip and promotes stacking fault and twin formation under dynamic loading
Deformation twins amplify strain hardening and maintain strength–ductility balance at high strain rates
Dynamic yield stress increases by ~30% over quasi-static values due to twin-mediated hardening
The cited evidence (E2, E3) directly supports SFE-driven twinning and dynamic hardening in this alloy system
